case_name: M. M. Ipoh and Others v Commissioner of Income Tax, Madras
respondent:
Commissioner of Income Tax, Madras
Supreme Court of India

26 July 1967
C.As. Nos. 1060-1064 of 1965, C.As. Nos. 1103-1107 of 1966
The Judgment was delivered by: J. C. Shah, J.
1.  Meyyappa, Alagammal his wife, and Chokalingam and Meyyappa (11) his two minor sons formed in 1940 a Hindu Undivided Family which traded in the name of "M.S. M.M.". The family carried on extensive business in money lending, rubber plantations, and in real estates in the Federated States of Malaya, Burma and India.
2.  The property of the undivided family was divided between the three male members on February 22, 1940. To Meyyappa  were allotted at the partition "business of the family" at Rangoon and at Karaikudi in the Ramnath District and three rubber estates in the Federated States of Malaya and some houses. Even after the partition Meyyappa continued to remain in management on behalf of himself and his two minor sons of all the properties 'and the businesses carried on by the famil
facts: Meyyappa, Alagammal his wife, and Chokalingam and Meyyappa (11) his two minor sons formed in 1940 a Hindu Undivided Family which traded in the name of 'M.S. M.M.'
The property of the undivided family was divided between the three male members on February 22, 1940.
In December 1941 Alagammal gave birth to a son who was named Chettiappa.
On April 13, 1950 partition was effected between Meyyappa and the minor Chettiappa by posting entries in the books of account of M.M. Ipoh.
Meyyappa acceded to a demand made by Chokalingam on behalf of the M.S.M.M. firm for a half share in the 'M.M. lpoh properties'.
issues: Whether the assessments on the 'Association of persons' for assessment years 1951-52 to 1956-57 are valid?
Whether Meyyappa acted on behalf of Chettiappa in forming the association?
petitioner_arguments: The Act sets out no principles and discloses no guidance to the Income-tax Officer in exercising the option.
The Act confers arbitrary and uncontrolled authority upon the Income-tax Officer.
respondent_arguments: The procedure for assessment is the same whether the income is assessed in the hands of the association or the share of each member of the association is assessed separately.
court_reasoning: The Court held that sub-s. (4) of s. 5 of Act 30 of 1947 dealt with the same class of persons who fall within the ambit of s. 34 of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922.
The procedure for assessment is the same whether the income is assessed in the hands of the association or the share of each member of the association is assessed separately.
holding: The High Court held that the income brought to tax in the assessment year 1951-52 did not accrue to an association of persons, but the income in the years 1952-53 to 1956-57 accrued to an association of persons formed by Meyyappa, M.S.M.M. firm and the minor Chettiappa.

The High Court accordingly by order dated April 3, 1961 answered the first question in favour of the assesses in respect of the assessment year 1951-52 and against the assesses for the subsequent five assessment years.
